LESSON: PHONIC DEVELOPMENT

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: READING
Topic 3.2: Phonic development

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Phonic development. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. develop knowledge of 4 lessons
2. build phonemes into syllables
3. read and sound syllables
4. relate syllables to their sounds 136 e) appreciate the use of syllables to form words consonant clusters right intonation

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. develop knowledge of 4 lessons
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to develop knowledge of 4 lessons. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. build phonemes into syllables
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to build phonemes into syllables. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. read and sound syllables
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to read and sound syllables. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

4. relate syllables to their sounds 136 e) appreciate the use of syllables to form words consonant clusters right intonation
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to relate syllables to their sounds 136 e) appreciate the use of syllables to form words consonant clusters right intonation. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Phonic development.
2. Explain Phonic development to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Phonic development.
4. Show that you can: develop knowledge of 4 lessons
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Phonic development. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Phonic development important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. develop knowledge of 4 lessons
2. build phonemes into syllables
3. read and sound syllables
4. relate syllables to their sounds 136 e) appreciate the use of syllables to form words consonant clusters right intonation

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
